change.title: stripe-node (npm) 23.0.0: pins 2026-09-30.endive; removes Stripe.constructEventWithoutVerification, ErrorType export, V2List V1-only fields

source.quote: Removed the function `Stripe.constructEventWithoutVerification()` that was mistakenly added in version 22.5.0 of this package.

tasks.reasoning:
The repo uses stripe-node 18.1.0 with apiVersion pinned to 2025-04-30.basil, so nothing breaks today. Stripe keeps old versions working, but every newer major (19–23) applies to the installed SDK, and 23 pins 2026-09-30.endive. Doing the move as one PR means: bump stripe to 23, change the pinned apiVersion literal to endive, remove payment_method_types from the Checkout Session create, switch any Stripe(...) call to new Stripe(...), and fix any type breaks in the subscription reads and webhook handling. The response handling was not read by the scan, so the migration agent should check which Subscription fields lib/stripe.ts and syncStripeDataToKV.ts read. ui_mode is not passed, so the Dahlia ui_mode enum change should not need an edit.
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- stripe:2026-09-30-endive-api-version (api-version): New API major 2026-09-30.endive carries breaking changes; pin it via Stripe-Version or upgrade SDKs (node 23, python 16, go v87), effective 2026-09-30. stripe-node 23 pins 2026-09-30.endive. The typed apiVersion literal '2025-04-30.basil' in lib/stripe/getOrCreateCustomer.ts:5 must move to endive in the same edit, so the API-version bump and the SDK bump are one move.
  Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/endive.md
  "As the first version in the Endive release, `2026-09-30.endive` introduces both breaking changes and new features."
- stripe:2026-09-30-remove-payment-method-types-checkout (field-removed): payment_method_types removed from Checkout Sessions create, and paymentMethodTypes option removed from Elements deferred intents (Stripe.js), effective 2026-09-30. checkout.sessions.create at app/api/stripe/generate-checkout/route.ts:62 passes payment_method_types. That only fails once the request goes out on endive, which is what this upgrade does, so the parameter is dropped as part of it (rely on dynamic payment methods or Dashboard settings).
  Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/endive.md
  "We [removed the `payment_method_types` parameter from Checkout Sessions]"
- stripe:2026-03-25-dahlia-api-version (api-version): API major 2026-03-25.dahlia with breaking changes (Checkout ui_mode enum values, events_from on event destinations, Capabilities risk requirements, Stripe.js method removals), effective 2026-03-25. Moving from basil to endive passes through Dahlia's breaking changes. They only apply when the pinned version moves, which this upgrade does.
  Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/dahlia.md
  "As the first version in the Dahlia release, `2026-03-25.dahlia` introduces both breaking changes and new features"
- stripe:node-22-0-0 (sdk-major): stripe-node (npm) 22.0.0: Stripe is a true ES6 class (use new Stripe()), types reworked, per-request host override removed, effective 2026-04-02. This is an intermediate major on the path from 18.1.0 to 23. Clients must be created with new Stripe(), types are reworked, and the per-request host override is removed. Check how the client is constructed in lib/stripe.ts and the other route files.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/stripe-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "Stripe import is now a true ES6 class. Use `new Stripe()` to create a StripeClient instead of calling it:"
- stripe:node-21-0-0 (sdk-major): stripe-node (npm) 21.0.0: pins 2026-03-25.dahlia, drops Node 16, decimal_string fields become Stripe.Decimal, wrong webhook parsing method throws, effective 2026-03-25. This is an intermediate major on the path. It drops Node 16, turns decimal_string fields into Stripe.Decimal, and makes the wrong webhook parsing method throw. Verify that webhooks.constructEvent at app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts:20 is the right method for these v1 snapshot events.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/stripe-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "All `decimal_string` fields changed type from `string` to `Stripe.Decimal` in both request params and response objects."
- stripe:node-20-0-0 (sdk-major): stripe-node (npm) 20.0.0: pins 2025-11-17.clover; v2 array params use indexed serialization (may break mock-server tests), effective 2025-11-18. This is an intermediate major on the path. Its only change is v2 array param serialization, which this repo does not use; nothing beyond the bump is expected.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/stripe-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "This may break any unit tests that expect the latter behavior when setting up a mock server."
- stripe:node-19-0-0 (sdk-major): stripe-node (npm) 19.0.0: pins 2025-09-30.clover; parseThinEvent renamed parseEventNotification, v2 delete returns V2DeletedObject, v2 nullable props optional; 19.x deprecated (Files API timeout bug), effective 2025-09-30. This is an intermediate major on the path. It renames parseThinEvent and changes v2 deletes, neither of which the repo uses; nothing beyond the bump is expected.
  Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/stripe-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md
  "Rename function `StripeClient.parseThinEvent` to `StripeClient.parseEventNotification` and remove the `Stripe.ThinEvent` interface."

callSites.why: Pins apiVersion '2025-04-30.basil'. This must change to '2026-09-30.endive' to type-check against stripe-node 23.
checkout.sessions.create passes payment_method_types, which is removed on endive (400 error / type error).
webhooks.constructEvent: node 21 throws when the wrong parsing method is used, and node 23 removes constructEventWithoutVerification. Confirm this is still valid usage.
subscriptions.retrieve: check client construction (node 22 needs new Stripe()) and the subscription fields read under the reworked types and endive shapes.
subscriptions.list with expand: check that the expanded and response fields still exist and are typed the same after Dahlia and Endive.
billingPortal.sessions.create goes through the upgraded client; verify the client is constructed with new Stripe().
customers.create goes through the upgraded client and its typed params; verify it compiles after the upgrade.

## stripe-node (npm) 23.0.0: pins 2026-09-30.endive; removes Stripe.constructEventWithoutVerification, ErrorType export, V2List V1-only fields [Verified]

### Change

Bumped stripe to 23.0.0 (and @types/node to ^20, required by stripe's peer dep; npm ERESOLVE otherwise). Pinned apiVersion to 2026-09-30.endive in lib/stripe.ts and lib/stripe/getOrCreateCustomer.ts. Removed payment_method_types from checkout.sessions.create. Subscription reads already use items.data[0].current_period_*; clients already use new Stripe(); no constructEventWithoutVerification, ErrorType, or V2 usage. Added scripts/check-stripe-endive.js as proof check.

Files touched:
- `app/api/stripe/generate-checkout/route.ts`
- `lib/stripe.ts`
- `lib/stripe/getOrCreateCustomer.ts`
- `package-lock.json`
- `package.json`
- `scripts/check-stripe-endive.js`
- `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`

### Why

stripe-node 23 types only accept the endive apiVersion, and endive removes payment_method_types from Checkout Session creation.

> Removed the function `Stripe.constructEventWithoutVerification()` that was mistakenly added in version 22.5.0 of this package.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/stripe-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md

preparation.reasoning:
No codegen or workspace builds are needed: the repo has no postinstall/prepare/generate scripts, and next build and tsc work from installed dependencies. The only environmental need is placeholder env vars, since modules like Stripe, Groq, OpenAI, SendGrid and Upstash Redis may be constructed at import time during next build's page-data collection and throw if their keys are missing.
The build fails at page-data collection because @octokit/auth-app requires GITHUB_APP_ID at module load, and it is not among the harness-provided env vars. No codegen or setup step is needed; supplying the GitHub App env placeholders from .env.example (plus the other unset template vars) addresses the environmental cause.

review.summary: The removals named in the quote do not touch this repo. Nothing calls Stripe.constructEventWithoutVerification, imports ErrorType, or uses V2List; the webhook uses webhooks.constructEvent, which is unaffected. The real change is a jump from stripe 18 to 23 and from API version 2025-04-30.basil to 2026-09-30.endive, which crosses several API versions. The diff also removes payment_method_types from checkout, which the quoted change does not require. Typecheck and build pass, but the stripe-endive check only greps for the edits the agent made, and nothing exercises live API responses or webhook payloads. 'verified' overstates what the checks show.

concerns.issue: Line 65 drops `payment_method_types: ["card"]`. The quoted changelog line does not require this. Without the param, Checkout falls back to dynamic payment methods: whatever is enabled in the Stripe Dashboard (wallets, Link, bank debits, etc.). That changes the customer-facing payment options, and possibly async payment flows the webhook does not expect. I could not confirm that endive removes or rejects this parameter; check the endive changelog and stripe 23's CheckoutSessionCreateParams type. If it is still accepted, restore it or have a human sign off on the behaviour change.

apiVersion moves from basil to 2026-09-30.endive. Every response shape read by lib/syncStripeDataToKV.ts and lib/stripe.ts:62 now follows endive. That includes items.data[0].current_period_start/end, price.id, default_payment_method.card and cancel_at_period_end. Typecheck only proves the SDK types still have these fields, not that live responses populate them the same way. I can't confirm the endive version string from memory; verify it against stripe 23's ApiVersion type and the changelog.

Webhook event payloads are rendered at the API version set on the webhook endpoint in the Dashboard, not at the SDK's apiVersion. After this change, the Stripe.Event types describe endive while live events may still arrive as basil, or the reverse. The handler casts to `any` and reads `object.customer`, so the risk is limited, but nothing tested a real or fixture event. The allowedEvents list also still includes 'invoice.upcoming'; confirm it still exists in endive.

stripe 23 declares engines node >=20 and peer @types/node >=20; @types/node was bumped to match. The deployment runtime (e.g. Vercel's Node version setting) must be Node 20 or later. TypeScript is pinned at 4.9.4; typecheck passed, but stripe 23 may officially need a newer TS. The stale `@types/stripe` ^8 dev dependency is still present and could shadow or confuse types.
The root package name changed from "lamp-bot" to "work" and the root "name" field was dropped. This looks like an artifact of the agent's sandbox directory and should be reverted.
A build cache artifact is committed with a large regenerated diff. It is unrelated to the migration; it should be excluded or gitignored.

The check only asserts that the installed version starts with 23 and greps for the agent's own edits. It is tautological and proves nothing about runtime behaviour. It does not cover subscriptions.list/retrieve, customers.create, billingPortal.sessions.create, checkout sessions or webhook parsing, so it does not justify a 'verified' grade.

checkFirst: Decide whether removing payment_method_types from checkout is intended; confirm against the endive changelog whether the param is still valid.

Run a Stripe test-mode checkout end to end, then trigger customer.subscription.updated and invoice.paid. Confirm syncStripeDataToKV still reads current_period_start/end and price.id, and that the users row updates.
Check the webhook endpoint's API version in the Stripe Dashboard and decide whether to move it to endive alongside the SDK.
Confirm the production runtime is Node 20 or later.
Revert the package-lock name change and drop tsconfig.tsbuildinfo from the PR.

change.title: Stripe.js: payment request button deprecated; handleNextAction UI, canConfirm, address and billing-details validation behaviour changes in Elements

tasks.reasoning:
It is uncertain whether these apply. The repo renders a Stripe Elements payment form (react-stripe-js 3.6.0), but the scan did not record which Stripe.js methods or elements it uses. The Stripe.js version is set by the @stripe/stripe-js package, separately from stripe-node, so this needs its own front-end edit. The migration agent should read StripePaymentForm.tsx for PaymentRequestButtonElement, handleCardPayment-style deprecated methods, initCheckout/initEmbeddedCheckout, and code that relies on elements.update() returning synchronously. It should then upgrade @stripe/stripe-js and @stripe/react-stripe-js and adapt any matches. If none are used, this is a plain package bump.
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- stripe:2026-03-25-stripejs-removals (other): Stripe.js: deprecated Payment Intents/Setup Intents/Sources methods removed; initCheckout and initEmbeddedCheckout renamed; elements.update() returns a Promise, effective 2026-03-25. Both are Stripe.js changes that only apply when @stripe/stripe-js and @stripe/react-stripe-js move to the Dahlia/Endive Stripe.js release. They are handled in the same front-end package upgrade, together with any removed deprecated PaymentIntent/SetupIntent methods or renamed initCheckout calls in the form.
  Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/dahlia.md
  "Removes deprecated Payment Intents, Setup Intents, and Sources methods from Stripe.js"

callSites.why: useStripe: the form may call Stripe.js methods (handleNextAction, deprecated confirm/handle methods, PaymentRequestButton) whose behaviour changed or which were removed.
useElements: Elements validation and canConfirm behaviour changed, elements.update() now returns a Promise, and the paymentRequestButton element is deprecated.

## Stripe.js: payment request button deprecated; handleNextAction UI, canConfirm, address and billing-details validation behaviour changes in Elements [Verified]

### Change

Bumped @stripe/stripe-js 7.0.0 -> ^10.2.1 and @stripe/react-stripe-js 3.6.0 -> ^7.0.1 via npm. The repo only uses PaymentElement, useStripe, useElements and stripe.confirmPayment, so no code changes were needed. Added scripts/check-stripejs-versions.js, which checks the installed versions and that the form uses no removed API. Typecheck and build pass.

Files touched:
- `package-lock.json`
- `package.json`
- `scripts/check-stripejs-versions.js`
- `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`

### Why

Stripe.js Dahlia/Endive removes the payment request button, the deprecated intent methods and the old initCheckout names, and makes elements.update() return a Promise. The repo uses none of these, so this is a plain package upgrade to stay on the supported Stripe.js release line.

> Deprecates the payment request button

Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog.md

| build | pass | pass | 0 |
| stripejs-versions | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- Runtime behaviour of PaymentElement and confirmPayment with the new Stripe.js in a browser was not exercised.
- Changes to canConfirm, address and billing-details validation could not be checked without a live checkout.
- Where Elements and loadStripe are set up could not be found in the repo (only StripePaymentForm.tsx uses Stripe.js). It may be missing from this repo or live elsewhere, so check that wiring.
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- The Stripe.js front-end packages move three majors (stripe-js 7 to 10, react-stripe-js 3 to 7). The PaymentElement flow is unchanged in the code, but behaviour comes from the new library versions.

preparation.reasoning:
No codegen or prebuild step is needed: the scripts are plain next build with a next-sitemap postbuild, and there is no prisma or workspace package. Dependencies with install scripts off are sufficient for tsc and next build. Only placeholder env vars are provided, since API clients like Stripe, OpenAI and Groq may be instantiated at module load during the build's page data collection.
The build fails while collecting page data because the @octokit/auth-app constructor throws 'privateKey option is required'. This happens when routes are loaded, since GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY is unset and the harness command does not export it. A placeholder value fixes that. No codegen or build steps are needed: there is no prisma or codegen, and the postbuild step runs as part of the build. The SendGrid 'SG.' message is only a warning. The other variables come from .env.example and are added defensively so module loading does not fail.

review.summary: The repo never used the payment request button. `components/payment/StripePaymentForm.tsx` uses `PaymentElement`, `useStripe`/`useElements` and `stripe.confirmPayment`, so the deprecation itself needs no code change. Instead the PR bumps `@stripe/stripe-js` across three majors (7→10) and `@stripe/react-stripe-js` across four (3→7). That brings in the Elements behaviour changes the changelog names: handleNextAction UI, canConfirm, and address and billing-details validation. Nothing here exercises that at runtime. The lockfile also carries unrelated churn, and a build artifact (`tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`) is committed. The 'verified' grade rests on typecheck, build and a check script the agent wrote itself. That script only reads version strings and greps one file for removed API names. It does not show the checkout flow still works.

concerns.issue: The version bump goes beyond what the API change forces: nothing in the repo uses PaymentRequestButton. A multi-major jump changes PaymentElement runtime behaviour, including billing-details/address validation and next-action (3DS) UI, on the live payment path. Typecheck and build cannot catch that. I could not confirm that stripe-js 10.2.1 and react-stripe-js 7.0.1 exist or check their release notes; verify on npm and in the packages' CHANGELOGs.

Newer stripe-js majors pin a specific Stripe.js release, which may imply a Stripe API version. The server uses `stripe` ^18. Check that PaymentIntents created server-side still confirm cleanly with the client's pinned Stripe.js/API version. Also check that the Elements provider's options still match the new types and behaviour; that provider is in a file not shown here.

The root package name changed from "lamp-bot" to "work" and the root `name` entry was dropped. This is an artifact of the agent's working directory, not of the migration. Regenerate the lockfile in the real repo, or revert those lines.
An incremental-build artifact was regenerated and committed, which makes the diff huge and hard to review. It should be reverted, and ideally gitignored.

The check script is self-written and circular: it asserts the versions the PR chose. It greps only StripePaymentForm.tsx for removed API names, so other files using Stripe Elements are not scanned. It also isn't wired into package.json scripts or CI.

checkFirst: Decide whether the 3-4 major-version bump is wanted at all. No payment request button is used, so the deprecation needs no change.

Run a test-mode checkout through PaymentElement, including a 3DS card (e.g. 4000002760003184). This confirms that the next-action UI, the `redirect: 'if_required'` path and the success routing still work.
Check the Elements/loadStripe setup file, where options and appearance are passed, against the react-stripe-js 7 and stripe-js 10 changelogs.
Revert the lockfile name change and the tsconfig.tsbuildinfo changes.

Stripe keeps old versions working, but every newer major (19–23) applies to the installed SDK, and 23 pins 2026-09-30.endive.
